identity.what_it_is: The northern half of Goodrington Sands beach, locally called 'North Sands' — a Blue Flag sandy beach on the English Riviera, tidal and backed by a promenade, separated from the larger South Sands by the Middle Stone headland.
identity.where: Goodrington, Paignton, Devon, TQ4 6LN, England — on Tor Bay, part of the English Riviera / English Riviera UNESCO Global Geopark.
identity.warnings: No harvested source uses the exact name 'Goodrington Sands North' or 'Goodrington Sands North Sands' as a formal place name — all sources describe one beach, 'Goodrington Sands', informally split into 'North Sands' and 'South Sands' by the Middle Stone headland. The slug may be over-specific; content should be clear it covers the north (promenade/tidal) section of the single Goodrington Sands beach, not a distinct named beach.

spike_candidates.statement: Goodrington Sands carries a Blue Flag clean-water award, yet a 2021 visitor review reported raw sewage discharging directly onto the beach.
spike_candidates.tension: The official 'safe, clean, family-friendly' Blue Flag branding sits uneasily beside a documented sewage overflow point on the same sand.

spike_candidates.statement: An 1809 Ordnance Survey shows a road once ran across what is now Goodrington Sands, where the tide now flows.
spike_candidates.tension: A beach marketed as a fixed leisure destination was, within recorded surveying history, dry land with a road on it — the coast has visibly retreated.

spike_candidates.statement: The rock exposures near Goodrington Sands skip the entire Carboniferous period, represented only by a single unconformity line in the cliffs.
spike_candidates.tension: Roughly 60 million years of Earth history are simply missing from the cliffs that beachgoers walk past every day.

facts.fact: Goodrington Sands is a sandy beach on the English Riviera at Goodrington, a coastal village on the outskirts of Paignton, Devon.
facts.quote: goodrington sands is a sandy beach on the english riviera, located at goodrington, a coastal village on the outskirts of paignton.
facts.source_title: Goodrington Sands - Wikipedia

facts.fact: The beach is split in two by a minor headland called Middle Stone, which has a bar and restaurants overlooking the bay, separating North Sands from South Sands.
facts.quote: the beach is split into two, south sands & north sands, by a minor headland, middle stone, that has a bar and restaurants overlooking the bay.
facts.source_title: Goodrington Sands - Wikipedia

facts.fact: Goodrington Sands measures 820 m long and 170 m wide, with a tidal drop of 4.4 m.
facts.quote: length 820 m (2,690 ft) • width 170 m (560 ft) • drop 4.4 m (14 ft)
facts.source_title: Goodrington Sands - Wikipedia

facts.fact: The beach's Ordnance Survey grid reference is SX 89359 59499, in Goodrington, Paignton.
facts.quote: grid position sx 89359 59499
facts.source_title: Goodrington Sands - Wikipedia

facts.fact: The beach's geology is sandy red Devonian rock, and it is operated by Torbay Council.
facts.quote: geology sandy (red devonian)
facts.source_title: Goodrington Sands - Wikipedia

facts.fact: Goodrington beach only exists because a sea wall was built to protect the railway; before that the whole area behind it was a salt-water marsh.
facts.quote: the beach only owes its existence to the sea wall put up to protect the railway as prior to that the whole area between the shore and the slopes 1⁄2 km inland behind the sports centre was a salt water marsh.
facts.source_title: Goodrington and Saltern Cove - OUGS South West

facts.fact: Grey pebbles on the beach are fossil Devonian corals, including the net-patterned alveolites and the branching coral thamnophora.
facts.quote: one common type is alveolites, which appears as a fine net and grew as a mat; the slightly larger net pattern is the coral thamnophora, a branching coral.
facts.source_title: Goodrington and Saltern Cove - OUGS South West

facts.fact: Near Goodrington, a striking geological unconformity means the entire Carboniferous period is missing from the exposed rock record.
facts.quote: the unconformity represents the whole of the carboniferous.
facts.source_title: Goodrington and Saltern Cove - OUGS South West

facts.fact: A 2019 academic paper describes the coastal outcrop between Waterside Cove and Goodrington Sands as revealing highly folded, cleaved Devonian beds unconformably overlain by near-horizontal beds.
facts.quote: between waterside cove and goodrington sands, a spectacular coastal outcrop reveals highly folded and cleaved devonian beds unconformably overlain by near-horizontal...
facts.source_title: South Devon, UK (Falcon-Lang, Geology Today, 2019)

facts.fact: A 2021 paper on the English Riviera UNESCO Global Geopark notes that the southern end of Goodrington Sands exposes Meadfoot Group Lower Devonian sandstones and siltstones folded into recumbent structures.
facts.quote: at the southern end of goodrington sands, south of paignton, is an outcrop of meadfoot group (lower devonian) sandstones and siltstones that are spectacularly folded into recumbent,...
facts.source_title: Trace fossils in Permian rocks of English Riviera UNESCO Global Geopark (Hart & Smart, Geoconservation Research, 2021)

facts.fact: An 1809 Ordnance Survey shows a road once ran across what is now Goodrington Sands, in a spot where the tide now flows.
facts.quote: the ordnance survey of 1809 shows that a road then traversed goodrington sands where the tide now flows
facts.source_title: On some recent discoveries in the submerged forest of Torbay (Pidgeon, Quarterly Journal of the Geological Society, 1885)

facts.fact: An 1861 geological account describes the Torbay shoreline from Berry Head to Goodrington Sands as composed of slates and limestones.
facts.quote: the north, and from berry head to goodrington sands on the south, are slates and limestones
facts.source_title: Recent encroachments of the sea on the shores of Torbay (Pengelly, The Geologist, 1861)

facts.fact: An 1861 travel account by naturalist Philip Henry Gosse describes stopping at 'the broad flat beach called the Goodrington sands' near Paignton.
facts.quote: drew up at the margin of the broad flat beach called the goodrington sands
facts.source_title: An hour among the Torbay sponges (Gosse, Good Words, 1861)

facts.fact: Beverley Holidays began in 1956 when Joseph Stanley Jeavons and his wife Marion bought 21 acres of farmland in Goodrington and moved from Wombourne, Staffordshire, with their three sons.
facts.quote: in 1956, they brought 21 acres of farmland in goodrington, on the outskirts of paignton with beautiful views over the bay, and moved from womborne in staffordshire with their three sons peter, alan and michael.
facts.source_title: Our Story - Beverley Holidays

facts.fact: Beverley Park, the holiday park adjoining Goodrington, opened in 1959 with just 10 caravans, a few tents and a shop, named after the Beverley Sisters.
facts.quote: the dream officially begun when beverley park opened its doors to happy holidaymakers in search of sun and sea air in 1959 with just 10 caravans, a few tents and a shop - with the famous beverley sisters as the inspiration for the name!
facts.source_title: Our Story - Beverley Holidays

facts.fact: In 1975 Beverley Park was awarded five-star status, an accolade held at the time by only four other parks in England.
facts.quote: in 1975, the successful family run park was awarded five-star status, an accolade which at the time had only be bestowed upon four other parks in england.
facts.source_title: Our Story - Beverley Holidays

facts.fact: As of 2025 Beverley Holidays is celebrating over 66 years on the English Riviera and is now run by the fourth generation of the Jeavons family.
facts.quote: fast forward to 2025 and our holiday parks are proud to be celebrating over 66 years of award-winning holidays on the english riviera
facts.source_title: Our Story - Beverley Holidays

facts.fact: Beverley Holidays is based on Goodrington Road, Paignton, Devon, TQ4 7JE, telephone 01803 843887.
facts.quote: beverley holidays goodrington road, paignton, devon, tq4 7je t 01803 843887
facts.source_title: Our Story - Beverley Holidays

facts.fact: Quaywest Waterpark, described as the UK's largest waterpark, sits virtually on Goodrington Sands and has eight waterslides plus a splash pool and swimming pool.
facts.quote: the uk's largest waterpark, quaywest waterpark, is also located virtually on the beach. eight waterslides, a small splash pool and a swimming pool make quaywest the perfect place to cool down.
facts.source_title: Goodrington Sands, Devon - The Beach Guide

facts.fact: At low tide, rock-pooling is Goodrington Sands' most popular activity, with the nearby Seashore Centre providing information on the rock-pool wildlife.
facts.quote: at low tide, goodrington sands' most popular activity becomes available: rock-pooling.
facts.source_title: Goodrington Sands, Devon - The Beach Guide

facts.fact: Dogs are allowed on North Sands all year round but are banned from South Sands.
facts.quote: dogs are allowed all year on north sands but banned on south sands.
facts.source_title: Goodrington Sands, Devon - The Beach Guide

facts.fact: A separate note on the same page says dogs are only allowed on the North Beach from May until the end of September.
facts.quote: for visitors bringing along dogs, it is important to note that from may until the end of september dogs are only allowed on the north beach.
facts.source_title: Goodrington Sands, Devon - The Beach Guide

facts.fact: Goodrington Sands has a seasonal lifeguard service, and visitors are advised to swim between the red and yellow flags when lifeguards are on duty.
facts.quote: goodrington sands has a seasonal lifeguard service.
facts.source_title: Goodrington Sands, Devon - The Beach Guide

facts.fact: A 2021 visitor review reported sewer overflow discharging directly onto the southern beach at Goodrington, with a second discharge point 500m upstream in the Goodrington stream.
facts.quote: the southern beach has sewer overflow discharging directly onto the beach in the middle of goodrington while another discharges 500m upstream in the goodrington stream that then meets the sea towards the southern end of the beach.
facts.source_title: Goodrington Sands, Devon - The Beach Guide (visitor review, M. Hunter)

facts.fact: A 2024 visitor review said the beach was 'only good for jumping off the stairs' and reported no lifeguard present.
facts.quote: only good for jumping off the stairs there is no lifeguard
facts.source_title: Goodrington Sands, Devon - The Beach Guide (visitor review)

facts.fact: The Beach Guide rates Goodrington Sands' water quality as 'good' (2 out of a possible rating), and the beach holds the Blue Flag award.
facts.quote: water quality ★★ good
facts.source_title: Goodrington Sands, Devon - The Beach Guide

facts.fact: For those not seeking watersports thrills, Goodrington Sands offers a beach restaurant and cafe plus sun loungers, beach huts and deck chairs for hire.
facts.quote: for those who aren't seeking an adrenaline rush, goodrington sands also offers a beach restaurant and cafe as well as sun loungers, beach huts and deck chairs for hire.
facts.source_title: Goodrington Sands, Devon - The Beach Guide

facts.fact: Facilities at Goodrington Sands include disabled access with a beach wheelchair, toilets, a cafe, a restaurant, deckchair/sunbed hire and a beach shop.
facts.quote: disabled access. beach wheelchair available. toilets. cafe/refreshments. restaurant. deckchair/sunbed hire. beach shop.
facts.source_title: Goodrington Sands, Devon - The Beach Guide

facts.fact: Goodrington Sands has about 1,100 parking spaces a 3-4 minute walk from the beach, plus a further 503 spaces an 8-minute walk away.
facts.quote: 1,100 (3-4 mins walk) + 503 (8 mins walk)
facts.source_title: Goodrington Sands - Wikipedia

facts.fact: Goodrington Sands is operated by Torbay Council.
facts.quote: operator torbay council
facts.source_title: Goodrington Sands - Wikipedia

facts.fact: Goodrington sits within the English Riviera, which is a designated UNESCO Global Geopark alongside Torquay, Paignton, Brixham, Babbacombe and Cockington.
facts.quote: the english riviera has a great choice of indoor and outdoor attractions and is a designated unesco global geopark.
facts.source_title: English Riviera - Torquay, Paignton, Brixham & South Devon

facts.fact: The English Riviera Walking Festival, covering the Goodrington/Torbay area, runs 16-21 June 2026.
facts.quote: the english riviera walking festival from 16th-21st june 2026, the english riviera walking festival will take over the bay once more.
facts.source_title: English Riviera - Torquay, Paignton, Brixham & South Devon

facts.fact: Torquay Tropical, a regional English Riviera festival, expanded on 11 September 2026 into a full two-day festival of music and carnival culture.
facts.quote: expanding to a full two-day festival and bringing an even bigger celebration of global music, carnival culture and shared experiences to torquay's seafront.
facts.source_title: Torquay Tropical returns bigger than ever for 2026 - Torbay Council

facts.fact: The International Agatha Christie Festival returned to Torbay from 12 to 20 September 2026, celebrating the region's most famous literary resident.
facts.quote: the international agatha christie festival returns to torbay from 12 to 20 september, with a packed programme of events celebrating the life, work and enduring legacy of one of the world's most beloved authors.
facts.source_title: Agatha Christie Festival returns - Torbay Council

facts.fact: A 2026 kelp forest study used Goodrington Sands (site 21) as one of its south Devon coast monitoring sites for the warm-water kelp Laminaria ochroleuca.
facts.quote: and site 21 ' goodrington sands ', all south coast of devon), and at two sites for l. ochroleuca (site 17 'fort bovisand' and site 21 ' goodrington sands '), respectively
facts.source_title: Temporal shifts in kelp forest structure and distribution largely reflect recent ocean warming trends (Salland et al., 2026)

facts.fact: A 2019 study for the Torbay Marine Conservation Zone found bait-digging effort at Goodrington Sands follows a similar seasonal pattern to nearby Broadsands, peaking in summer.
facts.quote: the seasonality of bait digging effort (mean number of diggers seen per hour) follows a similar pattern at broadsands and goodrington sands in that the effort peaks in the summer (1.5)
facts.source_title: Bait digging and hand gathering in the Torbay Marine Conservation Zone (Curtin, 2019, Devon and Severn IFCA)

facts.fact: Beaches near Goodrington Sands include Oyster Cove and Saltern Cove (0.4 miles), Fairy Cove (0.5 miles), Paignton Sands (0.6 miles) and Broadsands Beach (0.9 miles).
facts.quote: beaches nearby oyster cove (0.4 mi) saltern cove (0.4 mi) fairy cove (0.5 mi) paignton sands (0.6 mi) broadsands beach (0.9 mi)
facts.source_title: Goodrington Sands, Devon - The Beach Guide

facts.fact: A 2022 visitor review complained there was no clear demarcation between north and south beach and that dog-restriction signs were unclear.
facts.quote: no clear demarcation on which is south beach and which is north beach. dogs not allowed signs should be larger and clearer.
facts.source_title: Goodrington Sands, Devon - The Beach Guide (visitor review, confusing n smith)

facts.fact: Goodrington Sands holds an average visitor rating of 3.7 out of 5 from 77 votes on The Beach Guide.
facts.quote: rating: 3.7/5 (77 votes cast)
facts.source_title: Goodrington Sands, Devon - The Beach Guide

facts.fact: The beach's holiday park has been run by Beverley Holidays since 1956, now comprising three parks: Beverley Park, Beverley Bay and Beverley View.
facts.quote: beverley holidays (1956-present) (3 parks of beverley park, beverley bay and beverley view)
facts.source_title: Goodrington Sands - Wikipedia
